root_cause.text: `amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init()` in the amd-pstate cpufreq driver allocated a `cpudata` object at function entry but, if `amd_pstate_set_epp()` failed, it returned immediately without releasing that allocation, causing a memory leak on the error path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (ret) return ret;` to `if (ret) goto free_cpudata1;`, and the commit message explicitly states that on failure to set EPP the function “returns with an error code without freeing the cpudata object that was allocated at the beginning of the function.”

intent_record.how: On failure to set the default EPP value, the function now executes cleanup associated with free_cpudata1 before exiting, instead of returning immediately and potentially leaking or skipping resource teardown.
